checklist.fact: The City of Colfax, California (a small city in Placer County with a population just under 2,000) is issuing the RFP.

The City is procuring acquisition and implementation of a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system, including initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications provided by the selected vendor.

The City currently uses Fund Balance fund accounting software from Tyler Technologies (modules: Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, Business Licensing), with five users.

Key objectives include a streamlined package capturing financial transactions with budgeting and forecasting, effective reporting and data analysis, auditable records, and dedicated technical support during implementation and annual contract renewals.
Proposals are due Thursday, August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, by email plus an original hard copy, and late proposals will not be considered.
The RFP was issued July 1, 2025; written questions are due July 31, 2025, answers posted August 14, finalists notified September 11, interviews September 25, and contract award October 22, 2025.
The City's goal is to complete implementation and go live on July 1, 2026, in coordination with the new fiscal year.

Scope of work has four tasks: project management plan, software installation and implementation (including importing the prior 5 years of data), staff training with support for the first 12 months post-implementation, and ongoing technical assistance and support (including 1099 and W-2 e-filing).
Proposals are evaluated 45% on response to project goals and scope, 25% on technical support, 20% on fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% on information, qualifications and references.
The RFP states no budget or price ceiling, but reimbursable expenses cannot be unlimited and must be capped in the price proposal.
Respondents must provide documentation of measures protecting financial data and secure access controls (Attachment G), and disclose any use of workers outside the United States (Attachment C).

Attachment F (Software Abilities and Requirements spreadsheet) is a separate Excel document provided by the City and not included in this PDF; the City's standard contract is available only upon request.

specificity.reason: Components name concrete modules, migration steps, account segments, training formats and price schedules. C08 and C09 are more procedural, and C01 is thinner on downtime measures.

feasibility.reason: Weeks 1-20 and a July 2026 go-live are plausible. Gaps: very small City staff must support parallel running, Tyler extraction dependency is unaddressed, and 24/7 help desk staffing is unstated.

consistency.reason: Respects the reimbursable cap, no-exceptions rule, 15-day notice, Attachment C and the page and format limits. Minor strain: Attachment F is assumed to match scope, and the insurance limits are unconfirmed.

component_records.title: Mobilization, project management and governance
component_records.description: A named, dedicated project manager and technical staff are assigned from award, with a personnel management plan listing roles, hours of availability and escalation paths. We hold weekly meetings with Accounting and IT to monitor progress, budget and timeline, with a written status report and risk log issued after each. The plan is built backwards from a July 1, 2026 go-live so that configuration, migration, parallel running and training all complete before the City's new fiscal year begins, and it absorbs a start date soon after award and contract negotiation. We also document our understanding of the City's auditing and reporting requirements and the controls an auditor will test, so that design decisions are traceable to them.

component_records.title: Hosted accounting and financial reporting platform
component_records.description: We supply a cloud-hosted accounting and financial reporting system with complete implementation support, licensed on a subscription basis and hosted in our own SOC 2-audited environment. The configured scope covers every module the City uses today: Accounts Payable including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approval routing; Accounts Receivable; General Ledger; Payroll; Utility Billing; and Business Licensing. Transactions post systematically through approval workflows into a single general ledger, with budgeting and forecasting built into the same data model so that budget-to-actual and multi-year projections come from live transactions rather than spreadsheets. Report writing and ad-hoc analysis are delivered through a report designer and dashboards, and every transaction carries an audit trail with document attachment, period controls and retained history so records remain auditable for future reference. Ongoing services for all supplied applications — updates, hosting, support and annual e-filing — are included for the life of the contract, not just the first year.

component_records.title: Account structure design and financial report writing
component_records.description: We recommend and configure an account structure — fund, department, object and project segments with defined lengths and naming conventions — designed so that every transaction rolls up cleanly to the City's budget, its annual financial report and auditor workpapers. The structure is documented in a data dictionary and validated with Accounting before any data is loaded, and the proposal describes the customization available: segment count, code lengths, aliases, and the ability to add segments later without re-implementation. Working alongside City staff, we then write the City's core financial reports — budget-to-actual, balance sheet, revenue and expenditure detail, and utility billing summaries — and train power users to maintain and extend them.

component_records.title: Data migration of five years of history
component_records.description: We extract, cleanse and import the prior five years of financial history from the City's current Fund Balance system, covering general ledger balances and detail, accounts payable and receivable history, payroll history, utility billing history and business licence records. Migration follows a repeatable cycle — extract, profile, map, trial load into a test environment, reconcile to source control totals, then final load — with reconciliation sign-off by Accounting before cutover. We run the migration in parallel with configuration so that opening balances and comparative reporting are ready well before July 1, 2026, and we schedule cutover activity outside business hours to reduce downtime and operational impact.

component_records.title: Training, manuals and change management
component_records.description: We deliver personalized training and written manuals for the City's power users, tailored to the modules and reports they own, plus at least one recorded training session and a manual made available to all staff so new employees can be onboarded without repeat training. Training is delivered in person or virtually at the City's preference, with recordings retained in the City's own library. Because the City has a very small staff, we sequence training by role and run it against the configured test environment using the City's own data, so staff practise on realistic transactions before go-live.

component_records.title: Ongoing support, help desk and annual e-filing
component_records.description: A help desk and ticketing system is provided from go-live, with defined priority levels, response and resolution targets, and a portal where City staff can log, track and escalate tickets. The same support covers the first twelve months after implementation and continues through each annual contract renewal, with a named account manager and a dedicated technical support team rather than a general queue. Automated updates are applied to the hosted environment on a published schedule, and each release is accompanied by written communications describing software changes and their impact on City workflows. We support annual e-filing of 1099s and W-2s, including form generation, validation and submission assistance each filing season.

component_records.title: Price proposal and cost transparency
component_records.description: We submit a detailed price proposal on Attachment A covering the full scope of services, stating a total price for all services and deliverables, a total reimbursable expenses cap, and a total price proposal amount, with the relationship between the three figures explained so the evaluated price is unambiguous. The price is the total cost to the City to perform all requested services, including all materials, supplies and travel, with no cost left outside the total. Implementation fees and recurring fees are broken out in detail, license fees are broken out separately by license type and level of use, and support fees are listed with implementation-period costs separated from post-implementation costs. We also provide an estimate of costs and fees for any additional applications or third-party vendors we propose, and we cap reimbursable expenses at a stated figure rather than leaving them open-ended.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and data protection obligations
component_records.description: We accept all terms of the RFP as enforceable contract conditions under the City's General Contract Terms and Conditions, and we raise any proposed modification only during the question period rather than in the proposal. We observe the prohibition on communications about our proposal or others' during evaluation, and we accept disqualification as the consequence of a violation the City does not deem harmless. We provide documentation of the measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented — encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, multi-factor authentication, logging and monitoring, backup and recovery, and our independent audit report — mapped to the controls the City's auditors will test. We certify financial stability and no outstanding IRS or government liabilities, and we notify the Contract Lead within 15 days of any material change to those representations. We disclose in Attachment C whether any work is performed outside the United States and list those locations, and we give written notice to the City if personnel performing services relocate outside the United States. We bear all costs of preparing and submitting our proposal and of participating in interviews, and we will attend virtual finalists' interviews on September 25, 2025 if the City requires them.

component_records.title: Proposal production and submission control
component_records.description: A submission control plan governs the bid itself: written questions are lodged by July 31, 2025 through the City's stated channel, and the proposal is delivered as one signed original hard copy plus one digital copy emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov before 4:00 PM PST on August 28, 2025, with no FAX submission and no reliance on late receipt. The plan tracks the page allowance, the required tab order, the completed Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet, the licence-type and account-customization descriptions, the statement of where other applications or vendors are used, and the availability of virtual demos, so that no required element is omitted. It also holds the reference set with valid email addresses and the Attachment D certification signed by an authorized representative.

items.text: The issuing body is the City of Colfax, California, a city of just under 2,000 people in the Sierra Nevada foothills of Placer County at the junction of Interstate 80 and State Route 174 between Sacramento and Lake Tahoe.
The City operates on annual budgeted revenues of $6 million with 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus 1 part-time/seasonal/contract employee, and its fiscal year ends June 30.

The City currently runs Fund Balance fund accounting software from Tyler Technologies with modules for Accounts Payable (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions, and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, and Business Licensing, used by five users.

The City is replacing its current system with a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting system and wants a streamlined package that captures financial transactions systematically and efficiently, including budgeting and forecasting.

The business drivers stated in the RFP are the ability to generate reports and analyze data for informed decision-making, the ability to maintain auditable records and documentation for future reference, and dedicated technical support during implementation and across annual contract renewals.
The RFP was issued July 1, 2025 under the title "Accounting and Financial Reporting Software" and directs all inquiries to a single contact.

The City seeks a single vendor to supply and implement a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system, with complete support for the initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications provided.
The City's stated goal is to go live on July 1, 2026, to coincide with the start of the new fiscal year, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.

Task 1 requires an approach and project management plan with weekly meetings to monitor progress, budget and timeline, a dedicated project manager and technical staff, understanding of the City's auditing and reporting requirements, and a recommended account structure for auditable reporting.

Task 2 requires software installation and implementation support including financial report writing, import of the prior five years of data for history, and collaboration with Accounting and IT to minimize downtime and operational disruption during the transition.
Task 3 requires personalized training and manuals for power users, at least one recorded training session and a manual for all staff, and support for the first 12 months post-implementation.

Task 4 requires ongoing technical assistance including automated updates and software change communications, support for annual e-filing such as 1099s and W-2s, and a help desk or ticketing system for prioritizing support.
The City intends to award to a single respondent for all items, though it reserves the right to make separate awards, not award certain items, or cancel the RFP entirely.

Proposals are scored on four weighted criteria: 45% response to project goals and scope, 25% technical support during implementation and ongoing, 20% fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% information, qualifications and references.
Written questions are due July 31, 2025, and the City posts its responses on www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025.

Proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, with the digital copy emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov and the signed original hard copy received by the same deadline; late proposals will not be considered and FAX submissions are not accepted.
Finalists are notified September 11, 2025, virtual finalist interviews (if needed) are held September 25, 2025, and selection and contract award are scheduled for October 22, 2025.
The City may select a finalist group to interview with City leadership or make a final selection without interviews, and price proposals cannot be altered or modified as part of clarification.

Proposals must include a completed Attachment F "Software Abilities and Requirements" spreadsheet, identify license types for different levels of use, describe account number customization, identify where other applications or vendors will be used, and outline availability of virtual demos.
The City may reject any proposal on the basis of fit, form and function as well as cost, and non-compliance with any individual requirement may lead the City to reject a proposal in its entirety.
Reimbursable expenses must be capped in the price proposal, as the City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses.

Proposals must not exceed 20 pages, with an additional two pages allowed for the cover letter and five pages for appendices, and must be submitted as one signed original hard copy plus one digital version.

The City rejects and will not evaluate any additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal, and objections or exceptions to the City's terms must be raised as questions during the question period rather than stated in the proposal.
Only written material in an Addendum posted on www.colfax-ca.gov is authoritative and binding; informal or oral communications from City personnel are not official.
Respondents must provide at least three references for similar services with valid email addresses, and failure to provide a valid email may result in rejection of the proposal.

Attachment C requires respondents to state whether any work will be performed outside the United States and to list those locations, which the City will evaluate for additional risks and costs before award.

Respondents must submit Attachment D certifying financial stability and no outstanding IRS or government liabilities, and must notify the Contract Lead within 15 days of any material change to those representations.

Attachment F is an Excel spreadsheet provided separately by the City and is not included in the RFP, and Attachment G requires documentation of measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented.
The City's stated goal is to go live on July 1, 2026, to coincide with the start of its fiscal year, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.
The City's fiscal year ends June 30, which makes a July 1 cutover the natural boundary for opening balances.

The City currently runs Fund Balance from Tyler Technologies with Accounts Payable (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing, used by five users.
The City operates on annual budgeted revenues of $6 million with 11 full-time employees, so the account structure must serve a small finance team without dedicated report developers.
The City's current system is Tyler Technologies Fund Balance, which is the source system for the five-year history import.
The City has 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, so training must be role-based and repeatable through recordings and manuals.
The City's business drivers include dedicated technical support during implementation and across annual contract renewals.
The City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses and requires any reimbursable expenses to be capped in the price proposal.
The City rejects and will not evaluate additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal, and objections must be raised as questions during the question period.
Finalists are notified September 11, 2025 and virtual finalist interviews, if needed, are held September 25, 2025.

Proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, with a digital copy emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov and a signed original hard copy received by the same deadline; late proposals are not considered and FAX is not accepted.
Written questions are due July 31, 2025, with City responses posted on www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025.
The replacement system is assumed to cover all six modules the City uses today, including Utility Billing and Business Licensing, rather than treating any as out of scope.
Licensing is assumed to be based on the City's current five named users with headroom to add users at a published per-user rate, since the RFP does not state a required user count.
July 1, 2026 is treated as a committed go-live milestone in the implementation plan, with a contingency path if award or negotiation slips past October 2025.
The twelve months of post-implementation support is assumed to be included in the base recurring price and to start at go-live, not at contract signature.

The five-year history import is assumed to cover general ledger detail and balances plus AP, AR, payroll, utility billing and business licence records, with the vendor performing extraction and cleansing from the City's current system.
Reimbursable expenses are assumed to be capped at a stated dollar figure with travel billed inside that cap, since the City gives no cap amount.
The total price proposal amount is assumed to be the evaluated price and to include the reimbursable expenses cap, with the total price for services and the cap shown as its two components.
The Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet is assumed to match the functional scope described in the RFP body, and it will be completed and returned with the submission.
Financial-data protection documentation is assumed to be satisfied by a SOC 2 Type II report plus a written control narrative and architecture description, since no standard is specified.
The 15-day notification deadline in the financial certification is assumed to govern over the 30-day figure, and notice is given within 15 days for the life of the contract.
The proposal is assumed to require both a signed hard copy and an emailed digital copy, delivered to the City's street address, to satisfy the conflicting submission instructions.

Insurance is assumed to be priced at commercial general liability and workers compensation limits customary for a California municipality, with certificates on Attachment E, pending the City's stated limits.
No additional applications or third-party vendors are assumed to be required beyond the core platform, so the additional-application cost estimate is presented as a schedule of optional add-ons.

Attachment F and G requirements not available before the deadline. The RFP requires a completed Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet and treats Attachment G as holding software application requirements, but neither document is in the RFP package. The bid team cannot confirm the functional scope it is committing to, and the price and Tab 1 narrative may be built against a scope that Attachment F later contradicts. If the spreadsheet is not obtained and completed, the submission is non-responsive. Attachment F is mandatory (R098) and is a separate Excel file the City provides, while Attachment G is listed as holding solution requirements; neither is in the PDF, so the scope is unknown until the City supplies them.

Conflicting submission instructions: hard copy versus email. One requirement demands a signed original hard copy and another requires the proposal and all attachments to be emailed by the same 4:00 PM PST deadline, and the RFP does not say whether the mailed PO Box copy and the street-address copy are alternatives. A bid that satisfies only one channel risks being ruled late or non-responsive, and a bid that misses the physical delivery loses the whole pursuit. R041 and R045 directly conflict, and the RFP also leaves the delivery address ambiguous; late or incomplete delivery is not evaluated at all under R048.

July 1, 2026 go-live is a goal, not a committed date, and the start date is undefined. The City's go-live is stated as a goal and the project start only as 'soon after award and finalizing negotiations', with award scheduled for October 22, 2025. If award or negotiation slips, the roughly eight-month window to configure six modules, migrate five years of history, parallel run and train compresses, and the bid team has committed to a fixed date in its plan. Missing July 1, 2026 pushes cutover into the City's fiscal year and forces opening-balance rework. The RFP does not make July 1, 2026 binding or fix a mobilization start, yet the proposed plan is built backwards from that date with only a stated contingency path if award slips past October 2025.

Scope of the replacement system and user count are unsettled. The RFP lists the City's current modules but never says whether all six — including Utility Billing and Business Licensing — must be replaced, nor whether five users is the licensed count or growth must be accommodated. The proposed solution assumes all six modules and five named users with headroom. If the City intended a narrower scope the bid is overpriced against competitors; if it expects more users or modules, the fixed price is understated. R008 and R002 do not settle module scope or licensing basis, and the solution's assumptions on both are inferences from the current five-user Fund Balance deployment.

Financial-certification notification deadline conflict (15 vs 30 days). The RFP imposes two different deadlines for notifying the City of a material change to the financial condition certification — 30 days in one clause and 15 days in another. Operating to the wrong figure during the contract is a breach of a contractual notice obligation, and the certification is a continuing representation for the life of the contract. R096 and R136 state different periods for the same duty, and the RFP does not say which governs; the proposed solution assumes 15 days, which is an assumption rather than a settled term.

Attachment E and Attachment G referenced but not supplied. Attachment E is cited for the insurance certification and key personnel experience, and Attachment G for key personnel experience and software application requirements, but neither is in the RFP. The bid team cannot complete the insurance certification or the personnel-experience tab in the form the City expects, and an incomplete attachment set is grounds for rejection. Both attachments are referenced at specific tabs and pages but absent from the package, and R054 requires every attachment that needs information to be populated.

Five-year data migration scope and effort are undefined. The RFP requires import of the prior five years of data but does not say which data sets, formats or source extracts are in scope, or whether the City or the vendor performs extraction and cleansing. The proposed solution assumes the vendor extracts and cleanses GL detail and balances plus AP, AR, payroll, utility billing and business licence records. If the source data is dirtier or larger than assumed, migration and reconciliation overrun the fixed price and threaten the go-live. R107 states only 'prior 5 years of data'; the effort turns on source-system extract quality and volume that the RFP does not provide, and the solution's assumption is an inference.

Reimbursable expense cap and evaluated price basis are not defined. The City requires a capped reimbursable allowance and three separate price figures — total price for services, total reimbursable cap and total price proposal amount — without saying how they relate or which is evaluated. The proposed solution assumes the total price proposal amount includes the cap and is the evaluated price. A misread here either inflates the bid against competitors or leaves travel and expenses uncapped and exposed. R085, R120, R121 and R122 require the figures but the RFP gives no cap amount and no definition of the relationship between them; the solution's reading is an inference.

Insurance limits and financial-data protection evidence are unspecified. The RFP requires proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability coverage 'including but not limited to' the listed types, with no limits, additional-insured status or certificate form, and requires documentation of financial-data protection and access controls without naming a standard. The bid team cannot price insurance or judge whether its SOC 2 report and control narrative will satisfy the City, and a shortfall discovered at award delays contract execution. R097 and R099 are mandatory but the RFP leaves the coverage limits and the acceptable evidence open; the solution assumes customary municipal limits and a SOC 2 Type II report.

Standard contract and General Terms not available for review. The RFP makes all its terms enforceable contract conditions and rejects any proposal that modifies them, yet the City's standard contract and General Contract Terms and Conditions are only available on request and are not in the package. The bid team must accept unknown indemnity, liability, insurance and termination terms, and any objection raised after submission is disregarded or disqualifying. R037, R025 and R026 make the terms binding and bar exceptions in the proposal, while the contract documents are missing from the RFP; the risk is material but the terms are likely to be conventional municipal language.

Twelve-month support period pricing and start point are ambiguous. The RFP requires support for the first 12 months after implementation but does not say whether that period is in the base price or a separately priced option, or whether it starts at go-live, acceptance or contract signature. The proposed solution assumes it is included in the base recurring price starting at go-live. If the City reads it as starting at signature, the bid absorbs several months of unplanned support cost. R111 fixes the duration but not the pricing basis or start point, and the solution's treatment is an inference; the exposure is bounded to a few months of support fees.

Twenty-page limit and mandatory content volume conflict. The proposal must cover goals and scope, technical support, fee proposal and schedule, qualifications and references, plus account customization, licence types, third-party usage and demo availability, within a 20-page limit with two pages for the cover letter and five for appendices. The page limit is phrased as 'should not exceed' while surrounding instructions are mandatory, so the bid team cannot tell whether an overrun is non-responsive, and cramming the required content risks losing points on the 45% goals-and-scope criterion. R043 is desired while R044 and R053 are mandatory, and the RFP does not say whether exceeding the limit makes a proposal non-responsive; the impact is scoring and rework rather than project failure.
